summary: Gate policy for choosing light, normal, and workpack validation without turning every task into heavy process.
description: A portable validation pack that helps agents choose proportional proof for small edits, normal feature work, risky architecture changes, and long-running workpacks.
plainLanguageSummary: Use this to keep small tasks fast and make big or risky changes prove enough before closure.
bestFor: Projects where agents either run too much validation or not enough
Teams that want light, normal, and workpack lanes
Brownfield projects where closure proof is inconsistent
notFor: Throwaway spikes where no durable validation policy is needed
Projects that already have a complete accepted validation-lane contract
userQuestions: Is this a light, normal, or workpack change?
Which command proves the exact behavior changed?
Does this touch public API, data, security, stack, migration, or architecture boundaries?
qualityBar: Risky work explains why it escalated.
Closure includes proof commands and results.
Workpacks track execution only; durable rules move to decisions, policy, docs, or memory.
agentUse: Load this pack during start, next, eval, and done surfaces.
Use light lane for narrow local edits, normal lane for bounded feature work, and workpack lane for risky or long-running work.
Never use process as a substitute for progress.

appliesWhen.summary: The project has more than one useful check and agents need to choose proportionally.
evidence: typecheck, test, build, proof, e2e, lint, or workflow commands exist
some checks are fast and some are expensive
closure expectations vary by task risk

appliesWhen.summary: The project uses missions, plans, workpacks, or multi-step agent execution.
evidence: docs mention closure, proof, lanes, or gates
agent work often spans several turns

avoidWhen.summary: No validation gate policy is needed for a disposable experiment.
evidence: no durable deployment or release surface

rules.title: Light lane stays light
rules.summary: Small local edits should use a compact brief, inspect relevant files, make the edit, run a focused check when useful, and update memory only when project truth changed.
rules.rationale: Agents lose speed and user trust when every typo fix becomes a process-heavy workpack.
examples: Run one focused test for a one-file bug fix
Skip policy updates when no durable project truth changed
antiPatterns: Creating a workpack for a tiny copy change
Running full proof for a harmless local rename

rules.title: Risk escalates proof
rules.summary: Public API, architecture, data, security, stack, migration, generated-artifact, multi-package, or long-running changes must explain escalation and run staged gates.
rules.rationale: High-risk changes need durable context and stronger proof so agents do not drift or close unsafe work.
examples: Use a workpack for a new queue stack
Run typecheck, relevant tests, build, and policy drift before closing architecture changes
antiPatterns: Closing a migration after only checking one changed file
Adding a new dependency without proof or accepted stack decision

rules.title: Closure records proof
rules.summary: Before closing, the agent must record which checks ran, what passed or failed, and what remains risky or intentionally deferred.
rules.rationale: Future agents need proof history, not vague claims that work is done.
examples: Closure says typecheck passed, UI build passed, and proof was skipped because no proof lane exists
Open risk is recorded as a finding or follow-up instead of hidden in chat
antiPatterns: Done message with no validation result
Ignoring failed checks because the UI looked fine
